native_result.query: In which century did summed social capital peak, what individual social capital components like gold, monument etc increase?
native_result.HypoA: From 1500 BCE onwards, Monuments Count and Copper & Gold increase simultaneuosly while summer social capital peaks?
native_result.HypoB: Summed Social Capital (ZCU_AU Copper&Gold + Zamber Amber + ZMonument Monument Count) peaks in the century bin starting at BCE 1400 (14th century BCE, 1400-1301 BCE; CE -1400; calBP ~3350-3250) at 4.238, tied in raw 100-yr-sampled values at BCE 1300 but resolved unambiguously to BCE 1400 by the interpolated century-binned series. The only social-capital component that increases around/after this peak is Copper & Gold (ZCU_AU): 2.540 at the peak bin, rising to a short-window (BCE 1300-1200) mean of 2.695 and to its own maximum 2.850 at BCE 1200 (two centuries later than the summed peak), before the whole complex declines after ~BCE 1100 (long-window mean 0.901, slope -0.004/century). Amber (peak-bin -0.010 -> short mean -0.295, long mean -0.614, own max 1.540@BCE 3300) and Monument Count (peak-bin 1.708 -> short mean 1.530, long mean 0.147, own max 3.949@BCE 2700) do NOT increase after the peak and decline in both post-peak windows.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Parsed comma-decimal z-values in capital.csv (authoritative), oriented by ascending CE, summed SocialCapital = ZCU_AU+Zamber+ZMonument per 100-yr bin. 2) Verified identity with time_series raw at 37 century points (max diff 0.0) and cross-checked peak with century-binned _inter interpolated sum. 3) Located summed-sum peak (BCE 1400, 4.238). 4) For each component computed value at total-peak bin, immediate ~200-yr post-peak window mean (BCE 1300-1200), full post-peak window (BCE 1300-500) mean, OLS slope per century over the full window, and own-peak century/value; classified increase by short-window rise above peak-bin value and/or own peak later than total peak. 5) Kept openness/demographic proxies (pollen PC1, kde/growth) strictly as context on the overlapping span.
